review_note: Independent mathematical comparison with pinned original statement in Stage A sites.tex:5049. Did not view any proof or unsafe source slice. The site-object covering set E and each represented evaluation functor F↦f^-1 F(V) are both stated as premises. The conclusion is precisely existence of a left adjoint f_! to f^-1; the representability condition is functorial for every sheaf F, not merely at one F.
statement:
Let $\mathcal{C}$, $\mathcal{D}$ be two sites.
Let $f : \Sh(\mathcal{D}) \to \Sh(\mathcal{C})$ be a morphism of topoi.
Let $E \subset \Ob(\mathcal{D})$ be a subset such that
\begin{enumerate}
\item for $V \in E$ there exists a sheaf $\mathcal{G}$
on $\mathcal{C}$ such that $f^{-1}\mathcal{F}(V) = 
\Mor_{\Sh(\mathcal{C})}(\mathcal{G}, \mathcal{F})$ functorially
for $\mathcal{F}$ in $\Sh(\mathcal{C})$,
\item every object of $\mathcal{D}$ has a covering by objects of $E$.
\end{enumerate}
Then $f^{-1}$ has a left adjoint $f_!$.
